const invokeMock = vi.hoisted(() => vi.fn());

}));

  getToolAlwaysAllow: vi.fn(),
  setToolAlwaysAllow: vi.fn(),
}));
import { PasteTool } from "./paste.tool";
const toolInfo: ToolInfo = {...};
describe("PasteTool review", () => {
  beforeEach(() => { vi.clearAllMocks(); state.userPrefs = { reviewBeforeInsert: true }; });
  it("passes the assistant-tool source through review and pastes the edited text", async () => {
    reviewTranscriptBeforeInsertMock.mockResolvedValue("edited text");

    expect(reviewTranscriptBeforeInsertMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith("agent version", "assistant-tool");
    expect(invokeMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith("paste", { text: "edited text", keybind: null });
  });
  it("cancels when review returns null", async () => {
    reviewTranscriptBeforeInsertMock.mockResolvedValue(null);
    await expect(...).resolves.toEqual({ canceled: true });
    expect(invokeMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
  it("pastes directly when review is disabled", async () => {
    state.userPrefs = { reviewBeforeInsert: false };
    await expect(...).resolves.toEqual({});
    expect(review...).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(invokeMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith("paste", { text: "agent version", keybind: null });
  });
});

You are working on a repository with multiple accepted pull requests (PRs) that need final review and cleanup before merging. The goal is to prepare these PRs for production release by addressing all outstanding feedback and ensuring code quality.

Instructions

Phase 1: Address All PR Feedback

For each accepted PR:

Fetch and review all inline comments and general comments

Fully address every comment (resolve or implement changes)

Fix all SonarCloud findings, including code duplication issues

Ensure all CI checks pass

Phase 2: Deep Multi-Pass Review2. Perform 3 complete review passes using the FULL-REVIEW.md checklist:

Pass 1: File-by-file deep scrutiny of logic, edge cases, and correctness

Pass 2: Review for security, performance, and maintainability

Pass 3: Final verification of all changes and consistency

Document findings and resolutions for each file

Phase 3: Prepare for Shipment3. Ensure each PR is fully ready to merge:

All tests passing

No outstanding review comments

Code meets project standards

Use your judgment to make any necessary adjustments (you have full autonomy)

Phase 4: Evaluate Rejected PRs4. Review rejected PRs/branches and suggest any that should have been accepted, with clear reasoning

Phase 5: Commit Cleanup5. Squash all commits in each PR into a single, clean commit with a descriptive message

No multiple commits cluttering the history

One commit per PR

Output Requirements

Provide a summary of actions taken for each PR

List any rejected PRs recommended for acceptance with justification

Confirm all PRs are squashed to single commits

Report any blockers or items requiring human decision

Constraints

Maintain code quality and project conventions

Do not introduce breaking changes without justification

Preserve original intent of each PR

Document all significant decisions

Then suggest any rejected pr/branch you think should have been accepted

Then the created pr should have only one squashed commit not cluttering multiple one

fn has_url_scheme(first_segment: &str) -> bool {
    let Some((scheme, _)) = first_segment.split_once(':') else { return false; };
    let mut cs = scheme.chars();

It uses _sqlx_migrations with version numbers. If a dev DB has versions 71-87 recorded (from the old build), and the new build only registers version 69 (or 88):_

If new version = 88: DB at 87 → applies 88 → tries to ADD COLUMN that already exists → ERROR unless guarded.

Runner semantics (open.rs):

Recorded version not in configured set → OpenError::Other → app shows error, file untouched (no quarantine, no run). This is the DOWNGRADE protection.
So if a dev DB has rows 71-87 and we ship configured {1..68, 69} → startup ERROR "created by a newer version" → app blocked (Other error surfaces to user).
Fresh/0.1.5 DBs: apply 69 fine.
This downgrade check is INTENTIONAL product behavior (protects users downgrading). If we collapse to 69 and someone (dev) has 71-87 rows → hard error. Options:

(a) Keep the recorded versions in the configured set even though files are deleted — impossible; configured set comes from migrations() which needs SQL text.

(b) Treat "recorded > configured but schema-compatible" — special-case: versions that are recorded but not configured are OK if... we can't know schema state.

(c) Purge + idempotent consolidated migration: change open.rs so recorded-but-not-configured rows are DELETED (retire) rather than error... but that defeats the downgrade protection: a real user on newer version with MORE migrations who downgrades → we'd purge their future-version rows → then run consolidated69... their schema already has everything (if they were on87) → 69 must be idempotent → schema matches0.1.6 build → actually WORKS for downgrade to our build! The downgrade protection exists so old app doesn't run against newer schema. With consolidation, our build's schema target = same as max superfix schema. A DB written by "even newer" (hypothetical 0.1.7 with version 70+) → purging row70 then running 69 (idempotent no-op if columns for 69 all present... but 0.1.7's NEW columns beyond69's target would remain in schema — app code tolerant? unknown). The error message says "created by a newer version of the app" — for TRUE future builds (versions > 88), keep erroring. For the specific RETIRED range (71-88 → collapsed into 69), this consolidation is a known migration-set rewrite.

    let configured: std::collections::HashSet<i64> = ...;
    let mut retired: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
    for version in applied_checksums.keys() {
        if !configured.contains(version) {
            // Migrations 71-88 were folded into the single post-0.1.5            // consolidation step (69) for the 0.1.6 release; databases
            // written by intermediate superfix builds recorded them
            // individually. Those rows describe schema this build already
            // includes, so retire them instead of treating the open as a
            // downgrade. Any other unconfigured version keeps the strict
            // behavior below (a real newer-release database must surface).
            if (71..=88).contains(version) {
                retired.push(*version);
                continue;
            }
            return Err(OpenError::Other(format!(...existing...)));
        }
    }
    for version in retired {
        sqlx::query("DELETE FROM _sqlx_migrations WHERE version = ?1")
            .bind(version)
            .execute(pool)
            .await
            .map_err(|err| classify_sqlx("retire consolidated migration", err))?;
        applied_checksums.remove(&version);
        log::info!("Retired consolidated migration row {version}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn migration_69_upgrades_legacy_1_5_x_db() {
        // Simulate a user upgrading from a 0.1.5 build (the last migration it
        // shipped was 68): apply and record every earlier migration for real,
        // seed era-typical rows, then open. The single consolidated step 69
        // must rebuild the post-0.1.5 tables, preserve the rows, materialize
        // the new defaults, and drop the retired is_enterprise column.
        let temp = TempDb::new();
        let path = &temp.path;
        let pool = connect_pool(path).await.expect("connect to fresh db");
        sqlx::query(
            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _sqlx_migrations (
                version BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
                description TEXT NOT NULL,
                installed_on TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                success BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
                checksum BLOB NOT NULL,
                execution_time BIGINT NOT NULL
            )",
        )
        .execute(&pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
        // Everything the 0.1.5 release shipped, applied exactly as the old
        // migrator wrote it; only the consolidated step 69 is left pending.
        for migration in migrations() {
            if migration.version >= 69 {
                continue;
            }
            sqlx::query(
                "INSERT INTO _sqlx_migrations
                 (version, description, success, checksum, execution_time)
                 VALUES (?1, ?2, 1, ?3, 0)",
            )
            .bind(migration.version)
            .bind(migration.description)
            .bind(migration_checksum(migration.sql))
            .execute(&pool)
            .await
            .unwrap();
            sqlx::raw_sql(migration.sql)
                .execute(&pool)
                .await
                .expect("apply 0.1.5-era migration");
        }
        // Era-typical rows that must survive the rebuild.
        sqlx::query(
            "INSERT INTO user_preferences (user_id, transcription_mode, is_enterprise)
             VALUES ('legacy-user', char(99, 108, 111, 117, 100), 1)",
